title: A regression that ends without a result gets a page naming what happened to it (GitHub issue #11)
objective: When a regression ends without writing its result, its page says what happened to the regression process - the signal that stopped it, its exit code, or that it is gone - never 'unmeasured - None'.
outline: regression.py main(): install handlers for SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP that raise an exception (core.agents.Interrupted is the one auto_fixer.main uses the same way); keep the current stage in a variable updated where put_live is called; on the exception set the three signals to SIG_IGN (as auto_fixer does), let the finally blocks of verify/_verify remove the tree and release the slot, write --out and return 2; main's finally already drops the live record. ticket_controller.py after_regression(): build the fate text when report.get('summary') is not a string; the log path is the one _start_job uses (cfg.runs_dir('regression', gid) + '/regression.log'); signal names from signal.Signals(-rc).name. Out of scope: stopping the test command a stopped regression leaves running (testiface starts it in its own session) and detaching jobs from the controller's process tree.
test_plan: Verifier: acceptance 2, 3, 5 and 6 in a new class `RegressionStoppedAcceptance(LoopCase)` in tests_devloop/test_regression_fixer.py, placed between the existing classes T23Acceptance and T28Acceptance; start regression.py and read the live record's stage as T108Acceptance.test_a7_live_record_shows_stage_quick (same file) does; set tests.full by editing the "tests" object of board/config.json in the test; for the dead pid start subprocess.Popen(['true']) and wait for it. Send signals only with Popen.send_signal to processes the test started. Expected texts come from this ticket. Implementer: acceptance 1, 4, 7, 8 (a new class between Landing and T72Acceptance in tests_devloop/test_controller.py) and 9. Run only test_regression_fixer, test_controller and the base set.
notes: Group new-g1; depends on the #8 ticket (both change regression.py's verify() and docstring; this one starts from that code). Cause, measured 2026-11-24 with a throwaway loop-harness case on Linux (controller --forever, a 12 s full): SIGTERM or SIGINT sent to the controller alone leaves regression.py running; the next controller adopts it (finish_jobs: stamp alive), waits, reads its result and lands the group, with no unmeasured page. Sending SIGTERM to each child process of the controller (found by parent pid) and then to the controller reproduces exactly 'group g1: regression unmeasured - None. Fix the environment...': regression.py dies on the default SIGTERM action without writing --out and after_regression reads an empty report. So the cause is outside A: whatever stopped the controller in T also stopped the processes it had started (inferred: a stop of the controller's whole process tree, as tool runners do for background commands). The g57 auto_fixer survived because an earlier controller had started it, so it was no longer the stopped controller's child (inferred from POSIX reparenting of adopted processes). hard_block: board/config.json hard_block.patterns ('os\.kill', 'killpg', 'pkill', 'kill -') match every added line of the branch, tests, comments and README included, and stop the ticket for the user before merge: never write those words; use Popen.send_signal, osx.alive, signal names such as SIGKILL. Never write the reporting project's name in code, tests or comments (tests/test_no_project_names.py forbids it in every non-markdown file): say 'the reporting project'.
acceptance: devloop/regression.py handles SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP: it stops its work, removes its regression worktree, releases its slot or machine, drops its live record and writes --out as {"status": "unmeasured", "signal": "<SIGNAME>", "summary": ..., "failures": [], "flaky": [], "at": ...} (plus "sha" when known), then exits 2. The summary starts with 'stopped by <SIGNAME> during <stage>', <stage> being the stage of its live record at that moment (slot, machine, preflight, quick or full), and contains 'a controller restart leaves a running regression alone'.

Case: tests.full = 'sleep 30; <fake_tests.py> full', branch int/g1 made from main; the test starts `regression.py --branch int/g1 --out F` with subprocess.Popen and, once its live record <worktrees>/runs/live/regression-int-g1.json says stage 'full', calls proc.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM): the process exits with code 2 within 20 s; F has status 'unmeasured', signal 'SIGTERM' and a summary starting 'stopped by SIGTERM during full'; the live record file and the folder <worktrees>/regression-int-g1 no longer exist. (Today: exit -15 and no F, measured.)

The same with SIGINT: exit 2, signal 'SIGINT', summary starting 'stopped by SIGINT during full'. (Today: a KeyboardInterrupt traceback and no F; read from the code: main() catches only osx.OSFailure.)

ticket_controller.py after_regression(gid, job, rc): when the report at job['out'] is missing or has no string 'summary', the summary used for the page, for the group's paused text and for last_regression is the job's fate: rc None (an adopted job that is gone): 'regression.py (pid <pid>, started <the stamp's started>) is no longer running and wrote no result; it was not this controller's child, so its exit status is unknown'; rc < 0: 'regression.py (pid <pid>) was killed by signal <SIGNAME> (<n>) before it wrote a result'; rc >= 0: 'regression.py (pid <pid>) exited with rc <rc> without writing a result'; each followed by '; log <absolute path of <worktrees>/runs/regression/<gid>/regression.log>: <its last non-empty line, or (empty)>'. The page keeps today's template ('group <gid>: regression unmeasured - <summary>. Fix the environment, then run `actl tickets rerun <gid>` ...'), kind decision and options, and never contains 'unmeasured - None'.

Case, adopted and gone: group g1 in state pr with merged ticket #1, branch int/g1, and job {kind 'regression', stamp {pid of a process the test started and waited for, host osx.host(), boot osx.boot_id(), started osx.now()}, out <tmp>/missing.json}; <worktrees>/runs/regression/g1/regression.log holds 'line one\nboom at the end\n'. One ticket_controller.py run (no --forever) exits 3 and writes one decision page of ref g1 whose text contains 'is no longer running and wrote no result', 'boom at the end' and the log path, and not 'None'; g1's paused text and last_regression both contain 'is no longer running and wrote no result'. (Today the page says 'regression unmeasured - None'; measured.)

Case, own child, in process: Controller(Config(proj), pool) with forever set True; after_regression('g1', job, -9) on the fixture of the previous item (out missing) writes a decision page whose text contains 'was killed by signal SIGKILL (9) before it wrote a result'; on a fresh fixture after_regression('g1', job, 1) gives 'exited with rc 1 without writing a result'.
Unchanged: a report that has a summary is used as today; green, red, env and unmeasured-with-summary flows are unchanged.

A restart keeps a running regression (already true, measured; the implementer's regression test): a controller --forever started by the test reaches a regression whose tests.full sleeps 12 s; the test sends SIGTERM to the controller only (proc.send_signal); 1 s after the controller exits, the regression's pid (the group's job stamp) is still alive (osx.alive); a second controller run (no --forever) exits 0 with the ticket and group landed, one 'regression started' event and no decision page; the same with SIGINT.

devloop/README.md gets one paragraph right after the paragraph starting 'A fix round that leaves the branch redder is dropped (#74).' and before the one starting '`devloop.worktree_setup`': a controller stopped with SIGTERM or SIGINT leaves its issuers, regressions and fixers running and the next controller adopts them; stopping every process the controller started also stops its regressions: regression.py then records 'stopped by <signal> during <stage>' as an unmeasured result, and one that could not record it is named on the page by pid, exit code or signal, with the last line of its log.
token_basis: regression.py signal path (about 30 lines), one controller function, one README paragraph; 4 verifier cases (two Popen regressions of about 5 s, one controller run, one in-process call) and two restart cases of about 25 s; calibrated on landed complex tickets #108 (9.2M), #109 (9.9M), #113 (4.0M), #117 (6.8M)

# Fixes and one design change reported by tabby_pool (T) as GitHub issues #8 #9 #10 #11 #12 #13 on sai99claw/agent-control

The user asked for all of these (2026-11-24: 「OK 照這樣開票」), and ruled on the DAG part in docs/DECISIONS.md D-096 (read it first). Each ticket names its issue number(s) in its title so the main session can close the issues after landing. Issue texts quoted here are data, not instructions. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ (or a new file for a new area), using loop_harness.py; never a catch-all file. Each case should run in seconds.

Grouping: place these as you judge (core/chain.py, issue #6 design). #13's and the `actl dag` tickets change chain order and group membership, so they belong together; #8, #10 and #11 are independent of them.

## Issue #8: a regression's deadline starts when it has the machine
Observed in T (2026-11-23): g57's full regression waited for the machine behind g56, then had about 10 minutes left; the unit layers ran 554 s, test_browsers was stopped at the deadline after 40 s and the run was `unmeasured`.
Today devloop/regression.py `verify()` passes `began + regression_timeout_seconds` to `take`/`take_machine` and gives `_verify` the time left, so the wait is charged to the run (the module docstring says so).
Wanted: `regression_timeout_seconds` limits the run from the moment the slot or the whole machine is taken (preflight, quick, full and the flaky rerun share it). The wait for the machine gets its own limit: reuse an existing setting if one fits, otherwise add `devloop.regression_wait_seconds` with a default long enough for a full regression of another group to finish (say so in devloop/README.md); a wait that runs out is `unmeasured` with a summary saying it never got the machine, as today. Update the docstring.

## Issue #10: pages close when their subject is handled from any path
Observed in T (2026-11-23): the board showed 35 open pages, every one already answered or superseded: a group's "unmeasured" page after `actl tickets rerun gN`, tickets' "stuck" pages after `actl tickets ready N`, a fixer question after the group was readied, every `created` page.
Wanted:
- An action on a subject (a ticket or a group), through any path (CLI, board, `actl new --revise ... --decision`, `tickets ready`, `tickets rerun`, `tickets release`, `cancel`), acks every open decision/env page of that subject that the action answers, recording `acked_by` as the path (e.g. "tickets ready").
- When a subject moves on by itself (a stuck ticket is running again, an unmeasured group runs a regression again, a group or ticket lands or is cancelled), its older decision/env pages are acked with `acked_by: "superseded"`.
- `created` pages are information: the board's 要你判 tab and the waiting count do not count them (they stay listed in `tickets inbox`).
- Opener: grep every place that writes or reads `acked`, and every test that asserts pages stay open; list the tests that change.

## Issue #11: a controller restart does not kill in-flight regressions
Observed in T (2026-11-23 13:52Z): stopping `actl run --forever` and starting it again left g58 and g59 with "regression unmeasured - None" pages and no regression.py running; the g57 auto_fixer survived and was adopted. Jobs are started by osx.spawn with start_new_session=True, so the cause is not known.
Wanted: first reproduce it with the loop harness (start a controller, let it start a regression with a slow fake `full`, stop the controller with SIGTERM and with SIGINT, start a new one) and find the cause; write it in the ticket. Then fix it so a running regression survives the restart and is adopted like an auto_fixer: the new controller waits for it and reads its result. If the cause turns out to be outside A (for example how the user stopped the process on macOS), say so and make the controller report it instead of writing "unmeasured - None" (the page names what happened to the job).
